description: Looking for passionate and motivated members to join our NASA challenge team! If you enjoy innovation, teamwork, and solving problems, join us and let’s build something amazing together!
summary: Where on Earth could a crew rehearse for terrain like Jezero Crater on Mars or Mons Mouton on the Moon? Terraform-AI lets users explore seven planetary targets and compare each with twelve Earth patches in New Mexico, California and the central Andes. We use NASA elevation data to measure relief, slope and surface roughness over the same 20 × 20 km footprint at every site. The dashboard shows all 84 comparisons, with maps and measurements beside each ranking. For example, Andes D ranks first for Mons Mouton even though it has about 292 m more relief. Seeing that difference helps researchers decide which aspects of a terrestrial site warrant field testing.
details:
A crew training for a lunar traverse might need a place with a familiar mix of slopes and rough ground. Terraform-AI helps researchers find places to investigate and see exactly where the resemblance breaks down. Select Mars or the Moon, choose a named target, and open an Earth candidate to inspect its location, terrain measurements and rank among all twelve candidates.

We used Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA), Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) and Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) elevation rasters. A Python pipeline checks the inputs and resamples each region onto a local 500 m grid. The central 40 × 40 cells cover 20 × 20 km. We measure relief as the difference between the 95th and 5th elevation percentiles, median slope in degrees, and roughness as the median root-mean-square height difference from locally fitted planes. Mean elevation is displayed for context because each body uses a different height reference.

We divide relief by 200 m, slope by 3 degrees and roughness by 25 m, then compare the resulting three-feature vectors using equally weighted cosine similarity. We rank the twelve candidates by the unrounded index and display it on a scale of 0 to 100. California B ranks first for Jezero Crater at 99.768. Andes D ranks first for Mons Mouton at 99.922, yet their measured relief differs: 973.67 m on Earth versus 681.24 m on the Moon. A score measures the proportions of the three features. It does not estimate the probability of a safe landing or equivalent geology.

The three Mars targets are Jezero Crater, Nili Fossae and Antoniadi Crater. The four lunar targets are Mons Mouton, Haworth, de Gerlache and Cabeus. The Earth catalogue comprises four patches per region. A different catalogue or analysis scale could change the rankings. Ground strength, mineral composition, illumination and thermal inertia are outside the model.

The scientific pipeline uses Python, NumPy, Rasterio and pyproj. A React and TypeScript interface displays the saved results, Three.js renders the globes, and a map connects each rank to its actual Earth patch. Researchers can inspect the physical measurements before deciding whether a candidate deserves a field visit.
